name: Lettuce Green
lede: Lettuce green is a soft yellowish green named for lettuce leaves, with a long record in color dictionaries.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary defines *lettuce green* as the yellowish green of lettuce leaves [1]. The swatch is a moderate yellow green in ISCC-NBS terms [2]. The name has a long paper trail: Werner's *Nomenclature of Colours* of 1821 lists a lettuce green as number 57 among the greens, and Ridgway's 1912 atlas and the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 carry it too, though old plates are approximate [2]. Close neighbors are [[moss-green]], [[leaf-green]] and [[lime-green]], all in the family of [[green]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 235, 0.99 per cent, as photographed [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, as in 55 per cent of 141 paintings [3]. It peaks in the 1900s at 2.8 times the expected rate [3]. Its most devoted painter is Georges Seurat, who uses it in 10 of the 41 works we hold, 12.3 times the baseline, with Camille Pissarro next [3]. Among countries it is most over-represented in India, at 2.5 times expected [3].
